"fc42df58-65de-5a98-94e4-e78fc895ec49" :question/problem "Evaluate exactly.

$$
\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the exact value."] [:db/add "fc42df58-65de-5a98-94e4-e78fc895ec49" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=5 x$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(5)\,\mathrm{d}x$.

The differential is $\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\,\mathrm{d}u$. The outside factor is $3\cdot \frac{1}{5}=\frac{3}{5}$.

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=0\\x=\frac{1}{10}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{10}} \frac{3}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{5}\left(\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Endpoint values: $\arcsin{\left(0 \right)}=0,\quad \arcsin{\left(\frac{1}{2} \right)}=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arcsin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Evaluate the primitive and subtract lower from upper:

$$
\frac{3}{5}\left(\left[\arcsin{\left(u \right)}\right]_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)=\frac{3}{5}\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\left(0\right)\right).
$$

The exact answer is

$$
\frac{\pi}{10}.
$$"] [:db/add "fc42df58-65de-5a98-94e4-e78fc895ec49" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "fc42df58-65de-5a98-94e4-e78fc895ec49" :question/answer-fields $$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=0\\x=\frac{1}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{3}} \frac{4}{9 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{4}{3}\left(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\frac{4}{3}\left(\left[\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right]_{0}^{1}\right)=\frac{4}{3}\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\left(0\right)\right).
$$

\frac{\pi}{3}.

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0&\Longrightarrow u=0\\x=\frac{1}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} \frac{3}{4 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

$$
\int \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u=\arctan{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\frac{3}{2}\left(\left[\arctan{\left(u \right)}\right]_{0}^{1}\right)=\frac{3}{2}\left(\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\left(0\right)\right).
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{4}} \frac{2}{16 x^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{u^{2} + 1}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
